MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 219/2026 (Establishment, Withdrawal and Changes of Aids to Navigation, Fairways, Anchorages & Other Port Facilities)
Establishment, Repeal and Changes of Anchorages, Traffic Separation Schemes (TSSs) and Other Port Facilities
Owners, operators, masters, coxswains and persons-in-charge of vessels are advised that the following changes to anchorages, traffic separation schemes and other port facilities in Hong Kong waters will come into effect on 27 November 2026.
2. Seven new anchorages will be established, namely:
(a) East Lamma Anchorage; (b) Ha Mei Wan Anchorage; (c) Hei Ling Chau Dangerous Goods Anchorage; (d) Kellett Dangerous Goods Anchorage No. 1; (e) Kellett Dangerous Goods Anchorage No. 2; (f) South-east Lamma Dangerous Goods Anchorage; and (g) South Lamma Anchorage.
3. The boundaries of the Kellett Anchorages No. 1 to 3, South-west Lamma Anchorage, South Cheung Chau Anchorage, Western Quarantine & Immigration Anchorage and Western Dangerous Goods Anchorage will be adjusted. The existing South-east Lamma Anchorage, South Lamma Dangerous Goods Anchorage and Tsuen Wan Dangerous Goods Anchorage will be repealed.
4. The Mirs Bay Dangerous Goods Anchorage and Rocky Harbour Dangerous Goods Anchorage will be converted into multi-purpose anchorages and renamed as the Mirs Bay Anchorage and Rocky Harbour Anchorage respectively. The Urmston Road Anchorage will also be converted into a multi- purpose anchorage.
5. The existing Yau Ma Tei Anchorage will be rearranged to form the Yau Ma Tei Anchorage No. 1, Yau Ma Tei Anchorage No. 2 and a private mooring area south-east of Stonecutters Island. Except with the permission of the Director of Marine, vessels exceeding 100 metres in length overall must not anchor in the Yau Ma Tei Anchorage No. 1, and vessels exceeding 50 metres in length overall must not anchor in the Yau Ma Tei Anchorage No. 2. The Cheung Sha Wan Designated Bunkering Area will be repealed and the South-east Stonecutters Island Designated Bunkering Area will be established.
6. The existing Recommended Adamasta Traffic Separation Scheme and Recommended Fan Lau Traffic Separation Scheme will become local statutory traffic separation schemes (TSSs). 7. Masters, coxswains and persons-in-charge of vessels are reminded to strictly comply with Rule 10 (Traffic Separation Schemes) of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972 when navigating within the boundaries of all local statutory TSSs in the waters of Hong Kong. 8. Owners, operators, masters, coxswains and persons-in-charge of vessels should refer to the relevant legislation and the latest nautical charts and publications for the applicable boundaries and operational requirements, and take account of the revised arrangements when planning and conducting vessel movements. Details of the Amendment Regulation can be found the following link: https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/2026/ln102!en https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/2026/ln103!en https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/2026/ln104!en https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/2026/ln105!en https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/2026/ln106!en https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/2026/ln107!en 9. For the coordinates and boundaries of the revised anchorages, please refer to the appendix of this notice. Information on the changes to anchorages, port facilities and traffic separation schemes is also available at the Marine Department website: https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/materials-and-publications/publicity-materials/ index.html Mr. Q. MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 214/2026 (Navigation Warnings & Related Information)
Cross Harbour Swimming Races and Closure of Landing Steps
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that swimming races across the Central Harbour from Wan Chai, Hong Kong Island to Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon will take place from 0700 hours to 1100 hours on 15 November 2026. About 4,000 swimmers, under the escort of guard boats, are expected to participate in the races.
2. Launches of the Marine Department and Marine Police will be stationed or patrolling in the Central Harbour before and during the event.
3. Masters, coxswains and persons-in-charge of all vessels navigating in the vicinity should proceed with caution and give a wide berth to the swimmers, and follow the directions given by officers on Marine Department and Marine Police launches regulating marine traffic in the vicinity.
4. As the marine traffic in the Central Harbour will be affected by the races, vessel operators are advised to adjust their sailing schedules in order to avoid obstructing the races.
5. To facilitate the event, the following landing steps will be temporarily closed:
(i) Public Landings at the starting/finishing points – from 0900 hours on 14 November 2026 to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026;
(ii) Kowloon Public Pier No. 1 – from 0900 hours on 14 November 2026 to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026; and
(iii) Kowloon Public Pier No. 2 to No. 4 – from 0500 hours to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026.
6. During the aforementioned closure periods, owners and coxswains of vessels are advised to use other landing facilities in the vicinity.
7. A drawing showing the route of the races and the affected landing step is attached to this Notice.
Mr. S.F. WONG Director of Marine
Marine Department Government of the HKSAR Date: 10 November 2026 Action File Ref.: L/M 704/26 in MD-HPS-F01-015-045-002

MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 85/2026 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring “B” mooring A17, A29, A35, B2, B4 A36, A38, A39, A43, A78
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. Further information on minimum safe manning levels on ships while in the waters of Hong Kong can be found in Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/proc/index.html)
8. Coxswains, owners, agents and persons in control of local vessels are advised to take the precautionary measures contained in the Marine Department pamphlet entitled “Measures to Enhance the Safety of Local Vessels During Passage of Tropical Cyclones” well before a tropical cyclone is approaching Hong Kong. The pamphlet is available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/publication/materials/pdf/hps_cyclones.pdf)

MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 60/2025 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring “B” mooring A17, A36, A43 B03, B04 A74, A77
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. Further information on minimum safe manning levels on ships while in the waters of Hong Kong can be found in Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/proc/index.html)
8. Coxswains, owners, agents and persons in control of local vessels are advised to take the precautionary measures contained in the Marine Department pamphlet entitled “Measures to Enhance the Safety of Local Vessels During Passage of Tropical Cyclones” well before a tropical cyclone is approaching Hong Kong. The pamphlet is available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/publication/materials/pdf/hps_cyclones.pdf)
